source.authors: Köhler H, Contreras RA, Pizarro M, Cortés-Antíquera R, Zúñiga GE
source.title: Antioxidant Responses Induced by UVB Radiation in Deschampsia antarctica Desv.

value: total ROS content and membrane peroxidation peaked at 3 h of UVB exposure (21.4 kJ m-2 d-1) and declined to initial levels over the next 12 h
method: hydroponic plants exposed to a daily UVB dose; total ROS and membrane peroxidation (MDA) measured across a 24 h cycle against white-lamp controls
conditions: Plants collected on King George Island (South Shetland Islands), cultured in vitro for 2 years, then 2 weeks in hydroponic Hoagland No. 2 solution under a low UVB dose (1.7 kJ m-2 d-1); UVB treatment from mercury lamps at a total daily dose of 21.4 kJ m-2 d-1, stated to be similar to field doses on King George Island (unpublished); control plants under a white lamp with residual UVB of 1.7 kJ m-2 d-1; sampled across a 24 h cycle (3 h, 6 h and later points); means of N = 3 replicates per treatment (plants per replicate not stated), two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post-test, P < 0.05; wavelength band of the lamps not stated in the text read. The same section reports that membrane peroxidation then stayed significantly higher in UVB plants than in controls (Figure 3B), that control ROS did not change significantly, that PSII maximum efficiency was only slightly affected (values nearby 5%, Figure 3D) and that the abstract describes no dramatic change in MDA. The paper says the work was "performed in triplicates", not independent experiments; growth at 16 C with 16/8 h light/dark; ROS and POD units are not given in the text read.
where: Results, first paragraph (text sentence citing Figure 3A)
quote: Total ROS content and membrane peroxidation showed a maximum peak of accumulation at 3 h of UVB exposure before gradually declining to initial levels over the next 12 h (Figure 3A).
note: Biochemical response to UVB in a wild Antarctic grass; the paper's later sentence says membrane peroxidation remained significantly higher in UVB plants than in controls, so the 'return to initial levels' applies to the quoted sentence's wording only. source.authors: Köhler H, Contreras RA, Pizarro M, Cortés-Antíquera R, Zúñiga GE
source.title: Antioxidant Responses Induced by UVB Radiation in Deschampsia antarctica Desv.

value: peroxidase (POD) activity rose rapidly in the first 3 h of UVB and reached ten times the control level after 6 h
method: enzyme activity assays of total peroxidases in plants under daily UVB versus white-lamp control, sampled across a 24 h cycle
conditions: Plants collected on King George Island (South Shetland Islands), cultured in vitro for 2 years, then 2 weeks in hydroponic Hoagland No. 2 solution under a low UVB dose (1.7 kJ m-2 d-1); UVB treatment from mercury lamps at a total daily dose of 21.4 kJ m-2 d-1, stated to be similar to field doses on King George Island (unpublished); control plants under a white lamp with residual UVB of 1.7 kJ m-2 d-1; sampled across a 24 h cycle (3 h, 6 h and later points); means of N = 3 replicates per treatment (plants per replicate not stated), two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post-test, P < 0.05; wavelength band of the lamps not stated in the text read. SOD peaked at 3 h with the ROS peak then fell; APX rose only slightly at 3 h and stayed higher to the end of the cycle; CAT was upregulated but less than the other enzymes (Figure 4). The paper says the work was "performed in triplicates", not independent experiments; growth at 16 C with 16/8 h light/dark; ROS and POD units are not given in the text read.
where: Results, Antioxidant enzymes paragraph (text sentence citing Figure 4C)
quote: POD activity rapidly increased in the UVB treated plant in the first 3 h of UVB exposure reaching a level ten times than the control plants after 6 h (Figure 4C).
note: Antioxidant enzyme response to UVB; no UVB-free dark control or wavelength-resolved dose is reported. source.authors: Köhler H, Contreras RA, Pizarro M, Cortés-Antíquera R, Zúñiga GE
source.title: Antioxidant Responses Induced by UVB Radiation in Deschampsia antarctica Desv.

value: chlorophyll a/b ratio fell temporarily by 9.8% relative to control after 3 h of UVB exposure
method: pigment ratio measured in plants under daily UVB against white-lamp controls across a 24 h cycle
conditions: Plants collected on King George Island (South Shetland Islands), cultured in vitro for 2 years, then 2 weeks in hydroponic Hoagland No. 2 solution under a low UVB dose (1.7 kJ m-2 d-1); UVB treatment from mercury lamps at a total daily dose of 21.4 kJ m-2 d-1, stated to be similar to field doses on King George Island (unpublished); control plants under a white lamp with residual UVB of 1.7 kJ m-2 d-1; sampled across a 24 h cycle (3 h, 6 h and later points); means of N = 3 replicates per treatment (plants per replicate not stated), two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post-test, P < 0.05; wavelength band of the lamps not stated in the text read. Photosynthetic efficiency (PSII maximum efficiency) was only slightly affected, by values nearby 5% (Figure 3D); the text does not state which time points were significant. The paper says the work was "performed in triplicates", not independent experiments; growth at 16 C with 16/8 h light/dark; ROS and POD units are not given in the text read. The abstract states chlorophyll content showed no dramatic change; the text does not say whether the 9.8% fall was significant.
where: Results, first paragraph (text sentence citing Figure 3C)
quote: In contrast, the chlorophyll a/b ratio presented a temporary decrease of 9.8% with respect to the control after 3 h of UVB exposure (Figure 3C).
note: The sentence opens with 'In contrast' and follows the sentence on sustained membrane peroxidation (Figure 3B). source.authors: Barrera A, Hereme R, Ruiz-Lara S, Larrondo LF, Gundel PE, Pollmann S, Molina-Montenegro MA, Ramos P
source.title: Fungal Endophytes Enhance the Photoprotective Mechanisms and Photochemical Efficiency in the Antarctic Colobanthus quitensis (Kunth) Bartl. Exposed to UV-B Radiation

value: photochemical efficiency (Fv/Fm) of endophyte-free (E−) plants was significantly reduced under UV-B compared with E− controls and with E+ plants
method: Fv/Fm (PSII maximum quantum yield) in E- and E+ plants under UV-B and no-UV-B control, factorial ANOVA of endophyte presence and treatment time
conditions: Plants collected at Arctowski Station (South Shetland Islands) in 2016-2017; clones with endophytes (E+) and endophyte-free (E-, made endophyte-free with the fungicide Benlate); 6-month-old plants kept 30 days in a growth chamber at 4 C, then UV-B treatment of 46 umol photons m-2 s-1 (10 uW cm-2) from narrowband fluorescent UV-B tubes (peak near 313 nm), controls without UV-B behind Mylar film; photoperiod 21/3 h light/dark; sampled at 0, 6, 24 and 48 h; results are means of three independent experiments, two-way ANOVA, P < 0.05; the article gives no separate high and low UV-B doses and no UV-B hours per day. The next sentence says the reduction was mainly evident after 48 h. In the control ANOVA of Table 2 the endophyte term and the time term were both significant (P < 0.0001) although the text says E- and E+ controls were similar; Table 2 gives F and P values only, with no pairwise letters. Under UV-B the endophyte-by-time interaction was significant (F = 85.26); Methods give ten plants per condition; Table 2 has five time levels although four sampling times are listed. The paper's two UV-B figures disagree: 46 umol photons m-2 s-1 and 10 uW cm-2 (the latter is about 0.26 umol m-2 s-1 at 313 nm by the auditor's calculation).
where: Results, photochemical efficiency paragraph (text sentence citing Table 2)
quote: However, E− plants exposed to UV-B radiation displayed a significant reduction in photochemical efficiency compared to both, E- plants under UV-B radiation control and to E+ plants in any of the UV-B situations (Table 2).
note: Fv/Fm decline is shown for endophyte-free plants; endophyte-symbiotic plants were protected, so the UV-B stress response is the E- result.
